standardized.notes: RFC 959 obsoletes RFC 765/IEN 149 and preserves a much longer ARPANET FTP genealogy.

operations.monitoring: Control replies and data-connection state expose transfer progress/errors.
operations.diagnostics: Active/passive data-path and later firewall/NAT interaction are major operational branches.
operations.failure_behavior: Control connection may survive across individual data transfers; representation/file-system mismatches can fail independently of transport.
operations.operator_interface: Command/reply control channel plus separately established data connection.

open_questions: Recover early ARPANET FTP implementations and PI/DTP process structure.
Trace active/passive and NAT/firewall adaptations as later operational branches.

sources.locator: RFC 959 Sections 1-2 and FTP/Telnet relationship discussion

notes: SFTP and HTTP download roles must not be encoded as formal FTP revisions. FTP is especially valuable as a fossil of heterogeneous host file-system and representation assumptions.
